{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZdZMwg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDEj64", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 39, "title": "Correct aligned CPU word-transfer accounting for internal RAM and I/O", "body": "## Problem

At `a665b477bb347a21285881732054252c76f410ef`, `bus.rs:128` consolidates selected ROM reads only. CPU RAM word reads/writes, stack accesses, interrupt entry and word/string I/O otherwise accumulate two byte-access charges regardless of alignment. Ordinary aligned workloads therefore consume excessive emulated clocks, changing their relationship to raster events, timers and audio. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

Account eligible aligned internal word transfers as one bus transfer and odd-address words as two, across WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal. Apply this consistently through ordinary CPU paths while preserving data, register effects, model gates and shared-clock scheduling.

## Context

The clean checkout and remote main match the baseline. Open Issues/PRs are empty; inspected closed history contains no equivalent completed correction. [Issue #23](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/23) explicitly deferred RAM/I/O timing after implementing live ROM controls.

Relevant paths are `crates/ws-core/src/{bus.rs,cpu.rs,lib.rs}`, CPU/device tests, original fixtures and browser compatibility scripts.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), §§4.1–4.3 and Table 4-1, establishes one-clock bus cycles, even/odd word-transfer distinctions, stack penalties and two aligned vector-table word reads. It describes a CPU core; console connectivity requires separate evidence. [Wonderful timer definitions](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/hardware-definitions/blob/46783132a59e576c11456f5997620594eca1c390/target/wswan/timers.xml) and [EEPROM definitions](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/hardware-definitions/blob/46783132a59e576c11456f5997620594eca1c390/target/wswan/eeprom.xml) identify internal word registers. [Ares bus classification](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/blob/c76aaffa6e69778baf9a66d1da04298ac2ed7d1d/ares/ws/cpu/cpu.cpp) corroborates word-wide internal RAM/I/O and byte-wide SRAM/cartridge I/O; its constants are not independent silicon proof. [WSTimingTest](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSTimingTest/blob/main/README.md) reports physical Color alignment effects but explicitly warns about unresolved pipeline effects.

Correction record: the old implementation assumption charges each byte separately except selected ROM reads. The corrected requirement accounts transfer width and alignment for internal words. The preceding sources explain the distinction; record any further evidence-backed correction with its old assumption, replacement requirement and rationale.

Scope excludes full prefetch, absolute instruction-cycle accuracy, aliases/open bus, ROM-width mismatch data and speculative external wait corrections. WSdev Memory_map/Timing/SoC returned 403; inaccessible text and snippets establish no requirements.

[Saved #37 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/a665b477bb347a21285881732054252c76f410ef/docs/issue-37-validation.md) and [PR #38](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/pull/38) report 110 core tests, 16 integration tests, one adapter test, fixture/build checks and both Chromium suites passing, with Coordinator acceptance review. Published PR reviews are empty. Tests were inspected, not rerun; commercial games remain untested.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Before implementation, record a source-backed transfer table distinguishing accessible internal RAM, documented internal word-register pairs, SRAM and ROM. Establish internal byte/even-word/odd-word bus costs of 1/1/2 clocks. Distinguish register width from valid byte-lane effects; do not infer that every adjacent port accepts word writes. Label unresolved console behavior explicitly.
- [ ] Apply transfer-aware accounting to RAM data reads/writes, existing instruction-operand word-fetch helpers, stack operations and interrupt vector/stack accesses. Cover MOV, read-modify-write, calls/returns and memory strings, including REP and DF. Preserve the existing explicit prefetch approximation.
- [ ] Apply equivalent accounting to immediate/DX word IN/OUT and INS/OUTS for documented internal word-register pairs. Preserve defined byte values, masks, side-effect order, error handling and reserved-byte behavior. Determine eligibility before side-effectful dispatch; unrelated byte operations must never receive a word discount. Keep cartridge I/O byte-wide and preserve existing wait controls.
- [ ] Add independent literal cost/data vectors for byte, aligned and odd reads/writes on all models, including Color/Crystal mono and color modes. Cover RAM availability boundaries, segment-offset and 20-bit wrapping, port wrapping, internal/cartridge boundaries and existing ROM width/wait combinations. No consolidation may cross a wrap or incompatible region. Distinguish bus costs from approximate total instruction costs; demonstrate baseline failures.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 timing cartridge using calibrated aligned/odd RAM and valid internal-port loops with independently derived relative expectations. Validate native and production Chromium/Wasm execution on all three models, including restart and fresh CPU-written markers. Account explicitly for line/timer observation quantization; do not tune expectations to current output or unresolved prefetch effects.
- [ ] Preserve three-model behavior, live A0 controls, firmware-free startup, interrupt/REP boundaries, LCD pipeline, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/cartridge/internal EEPROM, browser persistence and input/frame continuity. CPU timing changes must reach the existing shared clock once; DMA retains separate accounting without double charges. Preserve ownership/provenance and browser-local ROM/save handling.
- [ ] Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against production preview, including the new probe.
- [ ] Update hardware documentation, fixture provenance and validation evidence. Coordinator reviews the final diff and actual results against every criterion and resolves blocking findings before merge. Correct AI-authored technical mistakes using primary evidence without human approval or independent AI re-review; preserve relevant acceptance and never weaken requirements to accommodate incomplete code or failures.

## Optional validation

Compare additional lawful timing experiments or another browser engine. Report source inspection separately from execution. Proprietary ROMs/firmware, physical consoles and human gameplay are unnecessary for acceptance.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
